quickAnswer: Medway is nearly split between utility gas at 45.8% and fuel oil at 41.4% of occupied homes, and its 1.3% vacancy rate ranks 47th of 50. The biggest age band is 1980 to 1999, so many homes are old enough to need attention but not ancient.
body: ## A town almost evenly divided between gas and oil

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 4,539 occupied homes in Medway. Utility gas heats 2,077 of them (45.8%) and fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,880 (41.4%), a gap of just over four points. Against the middle town, gas is a little higher (41.9%) and oil a little higher too (36.5%). Electricity heats 433 homes (9.5%), bottled or tank gas only 99 (2.2%), which ranks 44th of 50.

That near tie matters at a replacement. Two neighbors on the same road can have different fuels, and a family on oil is never far from the question of whether gas is available, whether a heat pump fits or whether a new oil boiler is still the simplest answer. Oil ranks 21st of 50 and gas 24th, so Medway sits in the middle of the pack on both.
## The 1980 to 1999 band did the building

The median Medway home was built in 1976, a year after the middle town's 1975 and 29th from the oldest. The single largest age band is 1980 to 1999, with 1,731 of 4,598 housing units, or 37.6%. Next come 1960 to 1979 with 960 units (20.9%), 1939 or earlier with 916 (19.9%) and 1940 to 1959 with 587 (12.8%).

Homes before 1980 total 2,463, or 53.6%, which ranks 34th and sits below the 57.2% of the middle town. Pre-1940 housing is 19.9%, the 15th-highest share. So the town carries a clear older core alongside a big late-century block.

Newer construction is thin. Only 404 units (8.8%) date from 2000 or later and 186 (4.0%) from 2010 on, the 46th-highest share of 50. For anyone replacing equipment, that means most Medway houses were built before the tightest modern building practices, so a heating load assessment is the starting point for sizing, not the label on the old unit.
## Detached houses, a few apartments and few empty homes

Single-family detached houses make up 3,797 units (82.6%), 16th among the 50 towns, and owners hold 3,942 households (86.8%). Renters number 597 (13.2%). Buildings with five or more units hold 367 units (8.0%), and all multi-unit buildings together hold 616, or 13.4%.

Only 59 housing units are vacant, a 1.3% rate that ranks 47th, against 3.6% for the middle town. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $546,700, a little under the $579,150 of the middle town and 30th of 50. When owners tend to occupy their homes and values sit in the middle of the pack, a free written estimate before any work starts is a practical way to compare a repair with a replacement.
## A mill town on the Charles

Medway was first settled in 1657 and incorporated on October 25, 1713, as a farming community. The water power of the Charles River and Chicken Brook then fed cotton and paper mills, straw and boot factories and cottage industries. For about 170 years the town also included the land that is now Millis, which separated in 1885 as East Medway.

The oldest road, laid out in 1670, is now Village Street, and in 1869 all of the town's streets were formally named. Medway covers 11.5 square miles, 0.78% of it water, and Routes 109 and 126 pass through. Interstate 495 clips the southwest corner without an exit.
## Where the rebate comes from

Heat pump rebates run through the utility that serves the address. Which program that is for your house is worth confirming before you shop, and the [heat pump page](/cities/medway/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) shows how the numbers play out against Medway's fuel mix.

faq.q: Should my Medway oil boiler be replaced with gas?
faq.a: It depends on whether a gas main runs past your property and what connecting would cost. With 2,077 Medway homes on gas and 1,880 on oil or kerosene, the two fuels are close to even, so neither is the obvious default. Compare written estimates for a new oil unit, a gas conversion and a heat pump before deciding.

faq.q: My Medway house dates from the late-century boom. Is the heating system probably fine?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The 1980 to 1999 band is Medway's largest at 1,731 homes, and equipment installed since then may still be original or may have been replaced. Age alone does not decide it. A visit that checks condition, efficiency and sizing tells you more than the year the house was built.

faq.q: Why is it hard to find a rental in Medway?
faq.a: The numbers point that way: Medway's vacancy rate is 1.3%, 47th of 50 towns, and renters are 13.2% of households. For a landlord, a heating failure in a tightly occupied building is felt quickly, so having a plan for repair or replacement ready before winter is a sound habit.

faq.q: Which heat pump rebate applies to a Medway home?
faq.a: That depends on the electric utility that serves the address, so confirm it first. Programs differ by utility, and terms can change. Once you know the path, the weatherization condition and the installer requirement come next. Ask for a written estimate that names the equipment, the zones served and the size chosen.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Medway runs on two main fuels: utility gas in 2,077 homes and oil or kerosene in 1,880. A replacement starts with that fuel choice, and gas work brings a permit and a final inspection.
body: ## Two fuels, one town

In the ACS 2022, 2,077 Medway homes use utility gas and 1,880 use fuel oil or kerosene, with 99 on bottled gas and 18 on wood. Those first two groups are close in size, so a boiler failure on one street may not look like a boiler failure on the next.

A gas household usually replaces like with like and focuses on size, venting and the gas connection. An oil household has more to weigh: renew the oil boiler, convert to gas if a main is close enough, or add a heat pump. Oil ranks 21st of 50 here.
### Permits for gas equipment
Before a gas appliance goes in, a licensed plumber or gas fitter has to pull the permit, and an inspection closes the job. The building department can explain Medway's side of that process.
### Rentals

Medway has 597 renter households, 13.2% of the town and 33rd of 50. The state sanitary code (105 CMR 410.201) sets the floor for rentals in the heating season at 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F through the night, with heat normally on the landlord unless a lease says differently. General information only.
### Houses with a late-century heating system

Medway's biggest age group is the 1,731 units of 1980 to 1999. Systems in that group may or may not still have their first boiler or furnace, and an original pipe or duct layout can limit what fits. If a unit is being swapped, that layout decides what size and type fit.
### Calling in a hurry

A heating failure on a cold night is an emergency, and we take those calls 24 hours a day at (508) 786-8755. Free written estimates arrive before work starts, so the repair-versus-replace decision can be made with the figures in hand.

faq.q: Is oil still a reasonable choice in Medway?
faq.a: For some households, yes. Oil heats 41.4% of Medway homes, so service and fuel delivery are familiar. A new oil boiler can be the simplest swap when the old one fails. The alternatives are a gas conversion where a main exists and a heat pump for part or all of the load, and a written comparison helps.

faq.q: How do I choose between repairing and replacing a Medway boiler?
faq.a: Look at three things: the age of the unit, how often it has failed lately and what the failed part is. A single small part on a younger boiler is normally a repair. A leaking cast iron section or a string of breakdowns usually points toward replacement, and a written estimate puts both numbers side by side.

faq.q: My rental building loses heat in a cold snap. Who pays?
faq.a: Tenants should report the problem to the landlord in writing, and the lease decides who bears the heating bill. Owners who need a fast repair can call us at any hour, and the options come back in a written estimate.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Medway has 3,797 detached houses and 616 units in multi-unit buildings, including 367 in buildings with five or more units. Central air, ductless heads and a heat pump that does both are all in play.
body: ## Cooling a mix of houses and small buildings

Of Medway's 4,598 housing units, 3,797 are single-family detached, 185 are attached townhouses, 128 sit in two-unit buildings, 121 in buildings of three or four, and 367 in buildings of five or more. A detached colonial and an apartment in a larger building do not call for the same equipment.
### Detached homes

Detached houses have room outside for a condenser and usually room inside for an air handler or wall heads. A radiator-heated house is the one most likely to lack ducts, which makes ductless heads the natural candidate. With 37.6% of units built from 1980 to 1999, a number of houses may already have a duct system to build on, but that depends on the individual house.
### Townhouses, duplexes and larger buildings

In an attached home, the condenser sits near a neighbor, so placement and sound both matter. In a bigger building, the question is whether each unit can have its own system or whether a shared arrangement is needed.
### Electric homes

Medway has 433 homes heated with electricity, 9.5% of the total. For them, a heat pump replaces resistance heat and cooling in one purchase. See the [heat pump page](/cities/medway/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Summer problems that are not equipment

A house that overheats in a few rooms may have an airflow or insulation issue before it has a capacity issue. A unit that runs constantly but never cools could be low on refrigerant, blocked at the coil, or simply too small for the space. Diagnosing the cause comes before buying anything.
### Sizing

Cooling load depends on windows, sun exposure, insulation and how many people use the space. A unit sized for the biggest heat wave of a decade may waste power the rest of the year, so a measured load is better than a guess.

faq.q: Can a Medway house with radiators have central air?
faq.a: It can, but only if ducts are added, which means finding space for runs and an air handler. Many radiator-heated houses are better served by ductless heads that need only a small hole through the wall for each line set. The right answer depends on the house, and a site visit settles it.

faq.q: My condo in a larger Medway building wants cooling. What are my options?
faq.a: Usually a ductless system sized to your unit, or a through-wall or window solution if the association restricts exterior equipment. Check the building rules on condenser placement and noise before ordering. A written estimate should show where the outdoor unit would sit and how the line set would be routed.

faq.q: Should one heat pump handle both heating and cooling?
faq.a: In many homes it can, and it is worth pricing. A heat pump that cools in summer can also take over much of the heating load in the shoulder seasons. Whether it can carry the whole winter depends on the model, the sizing and the house, so ask for the heating capacity at cold temperatures.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Medway has 1,880 oil or kerosene homes, 99 on bottled gas and 433 on electricity. Which rebate applies depends on the utility serving the address, and only 404 housing units date from 2000 or later.
body: ## Heat pumps against Medway's fuel mix

Mass Save's 2026 whole-home air source rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, provided the home is weatherized first. See the [heat pump services page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) for the full terms.
### Who has the most to compare

Oil heats 1,880 Medway homes (41.4%), and bottled gas heats 99 (2.2%). Both fuels are delivered, and a heat pump removes the delivery from the picture for whatever load it carries. The 433 homes on electricity (9.5%) can compare their current resistance or baseboard heat with a heat pump. The 2,077 gas homes are a different case: a heat pump there competes with a gas system that already works, so the interest may be in cooling and mild-weather heating.
### Age bands and the weatherization condition

The weatherization condition gives newer houses an easy pass. Only 404 Medway units date from 2000 or later, and 186 from 2010 onward, the 46th-highest share among the 50 towns. The much larger 1,731-unit band from 1980 to 1999, and the 2,463 units built before 1980, would normally go through a Home Energy Assessment to see whether weatherization work is recommended and how much.
### Ductless, ducted or both

Houses with radiators are natural for ductless heads. Houses with sound ducts can take a ducted unit that shares the existing runs. Some owners keep the oil or gas boiler for the coldest weeks and let the heat pump carry the rest, a hybrid arrangement that avoids relying on a new system alone in January.
### Sizing and the first estimate

We assess the home's heating load before quoting a system, and the estimate is free and written. The size of the heat pump should follow the house, not the old boiler's nameplate. A proposal that names the capacity at low outdoor temperatures is easier to compare than one that gives only a tonnage.
See the [cooling page](/cities/medway/air-conditioning-installation-repair) for the summer side of the same equipment.

faq.q: Does an oil home in Medway have the strongest case for a heat pump?
faq.a: Often it has one of the stronger cases, since oil is a delivered fuel and Medway has 1,880 such homes. Whether the numbers favor a heat pump depends on the house, its weatherization and the equipment chosen. Ask for a written estimate that shows a heat pump and a new oil boiler side by side.

faq.q: Does a Medway house from the 1980 to 1999 band pass the weatherization test automatically?
faq.a: No. The automatic pass is for homes built in 2000 or later. A house from that band would need a Home Energy Assessment recommending less than $1,000 of weatherization work, or completed recommendations from 2013 or later. Confirm current terms at masssave.com, since they can change.

faq.q: Can a heat pump work with an old forced-air system?
faq.a: Sometimes. If the ducts are sealed, sized for the airflow and in good condition, a ducted heat pump can use them. If they are leaky or undersized, the better route may be ductless heads in the main living areas. A site visit shows which applies to your house.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Medway has 3,942 owner-occupied households and 1,880 oil or kerosene homes. A yearly cleaning for oil equipment, a safety check for gas and a coil and filter visit for heat pumps keep a late-century house running.
body: ## Maintenance for a town of owners

Owners hold 3,942 Medway households, 86.8% of the total, and with few vacant units (59, or 1.3%), most houses are occupied through the year. That means a failure is noticed fast, which makes a planned visit before the season cheaper in stress than an emergency call during it.
### What each fuel needs

The 1,880 oil or kerosene homes need a yearly cleaning: burner service, a new nozzle and filter and a combustion check. A gas furnace or boiler needs a check of the burner, venting and controls. A heat pump needs its coils cleaned, its filters changed and its drain checked. Which of these applies to you depends on what is in your basement.
### Equipment from the 1980 to 1999 band

The 1,731 units from 1980 to 1999 are Medway's largest age group. Equipment installed in those years, or later when the original failed, has had many seasons of use. Corrosion, worn blower motors and failing igniters are typical late-life problems, and a tune-up is a chance to ask what is wearing out.
### Landlords and tenants

The 597 renter households live in buildings where the owner is responsible for the heating equipment unless the lease says otherwise. A fall inspection of boilers in rental buildings can head off a mid-winter call.

- **Late summer:** book the heating tune-up before the first cold week.
- **Spring:** cooling check, coil and drain.
- **Anytime:** soot, a burning smell or a carbon monoxide alarm means shut it down and call.
### Why spring matters too

Medway's 433 electric-heat homes and every house with air conditioning run their equipment in summer as well, and a cooling check in spring finds a clogged drain or dirty coil before the first hot week. Since the same outdoor unit often serves a heat pump in both seasons, one visit in each season covers its full year.
### Small habits

Replace filters on the schedule the manufacturer gives, keep snow off outdoor units and keep a clear path to the equipment. When you call, have the fuel, system age and nameplate details ready. If the visit finds a unit that cannot be saved, the [heating page](/cities/medway/heating-installation-repair) covers replacement.

faq.q: How often does a Medway oil system need a tune-up?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season. Oil burners collect soot, and nozzles and filters wear. Cleaning keeps combustion steady and reduces the chance of a shutdown during a cold week. With 41.4% of Medway homes on oil, the annual visit is a common routine here.

faq.q: Is a tune-up worthwhile on a gas furnace?
faq.a: Yes. The visit checks the burner, venting and controls for safety, and it tells you about the condition of the heat exchanger and blower. It also gives you an informed answer about how many more seasons the unit may reasonably serve before replacement becomes the better plan.

faq.q: What should I do if a carbon monoxide alarm sounds?
faq.a: Get everyone outside into fresh air, then call the fire department from outside. Do not go back in until it has been cleared. Once the emergency is over, have the fuel-burning equipment inspected before using it again, since the source needs to be found and fixed.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Medway's housing spans five age bands, with 1,731 units from 1980 to 1999 and 916 from 1939 or earlier. Older houses leak and tighter ones hold moisture, so the air problem depends on the era.
body: ## Air quality by age of house

The ACS 2022 splits Medway's 4,598 housing units into 916 from 1939 or earlier, 587 from 1940 to 1959, 960 from 1960 to 1979, 1,731 from 1980 to 1999 and 404 from 2000 or later. Each era moves air differently.
### Older houses

A house from before 1940 tends to leak through its envelope, and old ducts, if any, carry dust. If a renovation will disturb older materials, a qualified specialist should test them first. The 916 units in this band are the likeliest candidates.
### The late-century block

Houses in the 1980 to 1999 band are the largest group and are often tighter than their predecessors but looser than new builds. For them, bathroom fans, kitchen exhaust and a working humidity range are the practical checks.
### A town with a swamp in its story

Medway's history includes the Great Black Swamp at its geographic center, a tract so wet it could not be developed and which helped split the town in two. The town's land is only 0.78% water by area today, but a low or damp basement can still bring humidity indoors. Moisture control means finding the source, not masking it.
### What can be done

- Ventilation upgrades for houses that hold air in.
- A dehumidifier for damp basements, with the leak or drainage fixed first.
- Filters sized to the system's airflow.
- Cleaning for ducts that show visible dirt, mold or damage.
### Airflow and filters

Medway's mix of fuels points to mixed equipment: oil and gas furnaces with ducts, boilers with none and heat pumps. A forced-air house depends on the filter and return grilles for the quality of what it circulates, while a radiator house moves air mostly through the building envelope. The first sets the plan around the system, the second around ventilation.
### Testing

Measurements of humidity, carbon monoxide and particles describe one moment. They help most when paired with a plan for the source. If you also have a heating question, the [heating page](/cities/medway/heating-installation-repair) covers fuel and equipment.

faq.q: Should I worry about air quality in a house from the 1980 to 1999 band?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but ventilation is worth checking. Houses from that era are often tighter than older ones, so bathroom and kitchen fans should vent outdoors and run properly. A humidity reading in winter and summer shows whether the house is holding too much moisture.

faq.q: Does a humidifier help in winter?
faq.a: It can, if the air is very dry, but too much humidity causes condensation and mold. A humidifier tied to the heating system and controlled by a humidistat is easier to keep in range than a portable unit that someone must remember to fill. Aim for comfort without fogged windows.

faq.q: When is it worth testing indoor air?
faq.a: When there is a symptom or a suspected source, such as a musty smell, a carbon monoxide concern or visible mold. A test gives a snapshot of one day, so combine it with an inspection of the building. Fixing the source is what keeps the readings in range afterward.
